caption: Conceptual model as an activity cycle diagram. Cars alternate between being off site, waiting in one first-in-first-out queue and being plugged in; chargers alternate between free and occupied. The occupancy time is the whole plug-in stay (charging plus idle), which is why idle-time rules can replace chargers.

Process flow of one car in the simulation. A car takes a free charger or joins the queue; once plugged in it occupies the charger for its whole stay. The idle-time policies (P1-P3) shorten only the idle part that follows the end of charging.

Weekday sessions at the Caltech garage, 1 March to 31 May 2019. (a) Arrivals per weekday (65 days; dashed line = mean); Tuesdays and Wednesdays are the busiest days. (b) Arrivals by hour (bars) and the mean and median stay of cars arriving in that hour (lines; hours with at least 10 sessions): morning arrivals stay longest.

Arrival model. (a) Non-homogeneous Poisson rates for 48 half-hour slots (count per slot divided by 65 weekdays) for pooled weekdays, the Tuesday-Wednesday design day and +30% growth. (b) Time-rescaling check: the rescaled gaps follow the unit exponential distribution expected under the NHPP.

Stay (service-time) model. (a) Empirical distribution of the stay by arrival band, including stays over 24 h; these pools are sampled directly by the simulation. (b) Goodness of fit of the parametric candidates in each band (Anderson-Darling, parametric bootstrap with B = 500, so p cannot fall below 1/(B+1) = 0.002; mixLNk = mixture of k log-normals): no single family passes in any band, and only log-normal mixtures pass, in the 16-20 h and 21-04 h bands.

Idle time in the observed sessions (weekday sessions with a valid charge-completion time). (a) Share of each stay spent plugged in but not charging; most sessions are idle for more than half of their stay. (b) Mean charging and idle hours by arrival band.

FlexSim 2027 implementation at +30% demand with 45 open chargers. (a) 3D layout cropped to the model, with the object types numbered (source, queue, 52 single-capacity processors, closed chargers in grey, sink). (b) Dashboard panel of arrivals and departures per hour after the run (FlexSim default calendar).

Verification. (a) FlexSim with its own random streams versus the Python engine in the 12 key cells (30 replications each): every 95% Welch interval of the difference in P(W > 15 min) contains zero. (b) Known-answer test: with exponential stays the simulated M/M/c mean wait matches the exact Erlang-C value.

Validation at current demand with 52 chargers. (a) Mean number of cars plugged in by time of day: data with its 95% interval, the simulation and the analytic Mt/G/inf offered load. (b) Day-to-day dispersion of occupancy (variance over mean): the model varies more than the data, so its risk estimates are conservative.

Probability of waiting more than 15 min at +30% demand (m = 1.3) versus the number of chargers, with 95% confidence intervals from 200 replications with common random numbers. The decision rule selects the smallest c whose upper bound is at most 1%.

Sizing grid for pooled weekdays: upper 95% bound of P(W > 15 min) for every combination of growth factor and charger count (log colour scale). The black contour is the 1% target; the white dashed line marks the 52 installed chargers.

Feasibility frontier: the smallest charger count that meets the rule at each growth factor, from the simulation (pooled weekdays and design day) and from three analytic sizing rules. The installed 52 chargers meet the rule up to the point where the frontier crosses the dashed line.

Robustness. (a) Charger count selected when the 65 input days are resampled (50 bootstrap inputs x 20 replications at m = 1.3). (b) Share of drivers who would leave if they waited longer than their patience, by charger count.

Chargers saved by idle-time policies at +30% (m = 1.3) and +60% (m = 1.6) demand, relative to the no-policy requirement at the same growth. Driver behaviour under the policies (moving within g minutes, compliance share) is assumed, not observed.

Decision analysis under growth uncertainty (A0 keep 52; A1, A2, A3 buy 2, 6 or 13; A4 keep 52 with a voluntary 60-min rule; A5 the rule enforced by a fee). (a) Expected annual cost versus the probability of high growth. (b) Hurwicz criterion versus the optimism coefficient (lower is better).

(a) Annual cost of each option in each growth future (capital, maintenance and network fees, waiting and walking time, and policy administration). (b) AHP overall score of each option as the weight of the total-annualised-cost criterion changes (higher is better); this criterion includes the monetised waiting time, which also enters the service criterion.
